evidence:
Pairwise review of all 54 graded criteria (44 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual) plus 2 zero-weight gates. Strengths: the author has written explicit ownership splits for nearly every adjacent pair, e.g. hro_refusal_status 'Only the status is graded here; whether anything changed is graded in those rows' (functional judge.toml:200) vs hro_observer_readonly/hro_candidate_no_staff/hro_stale_refused; hro_interview_full 'Overfill by a multi-card move belongs to hro_bulk_places and by undo to hro_undo_full' (:110); hro_arrive_bottom defers multi-card arrival to hro_bulk_move (:65); hro_undo_restores 'The A2 undo in B(12) is graded only in hro_undo_conflict' (:245); hro_drafts defers box-clearing to hro_msg_compose (:380); hro_candidate_view defers privacy to hro_candidate_private and candidate replies to hro_msg_exchange (:389); hro_candidate_linked 'This row alone owns that link' (:407); hro_pol_live_thread defers scrolled-up placement to Functional (polish judge.toml:32); hro_pol_failed_send defers note drafts to hro_pol_session_resume (:50); hro_thread_access (Observer/Ingrid/Noor send replays) is disjoint from hro_observer_readonly (no message request listed). hro_activity vs hro_activity_refusals, hro_reject_reason vs hro_reject_hired vs hro_reopen, hro_mgr_late_stages vs hro_mgr_early_refused vs hro_mgr_other_job, hro_anonymous (401) vs hro_refusal_status (403/404/409) are complementary. No pair demands incompatible products: draft rules (hro_drafts, hro_msg_compose, hro_pol_live_thread, hro_pol_failed_send, hro_pol_session_resume) are jointly satisfiable by per-user per-conversation drafts cleared on send; at-newest vs scrolled-up arrival (hro_unread_counts, hro_pol_live_thread, hro_unread_scrolled_up) are disjoint conditions; candidate 403/404 policy matches hireops_rules.md section 1. Functional prompt.md:13,23 and the polish/visual prompts say not to deduct one observed defect in more than one row. Visual rows mirror the template's typography/colour/layout/hierarchy/craft split, so the typography anchor 'deliberate hierarchy' vs hro_vis_hierarchy overlap is template-inherited (Note only). Polish live rows that are 0 when no update arrives (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread) reuse live delivery as a policy-required positive control (REVIEW_POLICY 'A negative needs a successful control'), not a duplicate grade (Note). hro_job_open allowing places/manager to be 'evidenced by behaviour' in L/R couples it to hro_interview_full/hro_mgr_late_stages only when the app neither displays nor enforces the value (Note).
DEFECT (bounded): the candidate's own-conversation observable is a pass condition in three rows. hro_candidate_view (functional judge.toml:389) owns 'they can open and read their own conversations ... Fails if ... their own conversation is wrong or missing'. hro_candidate_no_staff (:182) states as a pass leg 'the candidate first signs in and their own applications and conversations load in that same session (the control)' and ends 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold'. hro_candidate_private (:398) likewise requires 'own applications and conversations load with their messages (the control)'. For candidate_private that control is justified (its leg 'asking for another application's conversation is answered as not found' needs a same-kind success). For candidate_no_staff it is not a same-kind control: its negatives are write replays (move, multi-card move, reject, undo, add-candidate, open-job, note) whose same-kind control, Rafael's identical success, is already listed; session validity needs only sign-in plus own data. So no_staff re-grades candidate_view's conversation observable, and its conjunctive 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold' conflicts with prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row', making the outcome depend on which instruction the judge follows. The row's own minimum ('A candidate who cannot sign in or receives none of their own data makes this row 0') shows the intended control is weaker than its first sentence. Not exercised: no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope).
counterexample: Weak-but-secure app: candidates sign in and their applications list loads with correct title/team/wording, but opening a candidate conversation fails (e.g. 500 or empty pane); every candidate replay of staff writes is correctly refused with 403 and nothing changes; Rafael's controls succeed. Correct grading: hro_candidate_view 0 (owns the defect), hro_candidate_no_staff 1. As written, hro_candidate_no_staff's stated control 'their own applications and conversations load' fails, so a literal judge also gives it 0 (an extra 1.0 of 59.5 functional weight lost for the same defect; hro_candidate_private also 0, which is defensible). A judge obeying prompt.md:23 instead gives 1, so identical apps can score differently depending on which conflicting instruction it applies.
suggested_fix: In hro_candidate_no_staff replace 'their own applications and conversations load in that same session (the control)' with 'their own applications list loads in that same session (session control; whether their conversations work is graded in hro_candidate_view)'.
